title: Chantilly Route 28 Dust in Air Ducts
headline: Why Chantilly and Sully Station Homes Still Blow Construction Dust
description: Why Chantilly and Sully Station homes still blow construction dust — builder fines, Route 28 film, and when to clean.

sections.heading: Builder-grade ductwork and the dust it was born with
paragraphs: Sully Station, Greenbriar, and Westfields developments went up during a sustained building cycle from the early 1990s through the 2010s. During construction, HVAC systems are installed and commissioned while drywall finishing, sanding, and painting are still underway. The air handler runs to dry joint compound. Gypsum dust — fine, white, and slightly calcium-rich — enters the return side and distributes through every supply trunk before the first homeowner moves in.

Post-construction duct cleaning is not a universal builder requirement, and many first-owner systems never get a full source-removal clean before move-in. The first filter catches some fines, but particles that settled on trunk walls beforehand can remain under later household dust. [EPA](https://www.epa.gov/sites/default/files/2020-06/documents/2019.07_tech_bulletin_duct_protection_during_construction.pdf) and [DOE Building America](https://basc.pnnl.gov/resource-guides/removing-construction-debris-ducts) treat construction debris in ducts as a known issue to prevent and remove. On Sully-area jobs we often see a chalky base layer under darker film when a second-floor supply comes off — consistent with unfinished construction dust that was never vacuumed out.

sections.heading: Dulles approach traffic adds a second, ongoing layer
paragraphs: Route 28 between Dulles and Centreville carries heavy commercial and passenger traffic. Corridor houses often show more road film on returns facing the highway than on sheltered sides of the same home — a pattern we see on walkthroughs more than a lab claim about any one chemical.

Chantilly houses west of Route 28 sit closest to that corridor dust. Over several years, register faces on the road side can gray faster than interior-facing ones. Standard panel filters help; they do not catch everything that settles deeper in the trunks.

sections.heading: HOA townhome dryer chases were sized for a different era
paragraphs: Many 1990s townhome dryer chases were sized for older appliances. Today's high-capacity dryers often push more air through the same elbows and vertical runs. When the chase is long or kinked, lint packs at turns, exhaust slows, and cycles run longer — a fire and humidity concern [NFPA links to dryer fires and failure to clean](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/research/nfpa-research/fire-statistical-reports/home-fires-involving-clothes-dryers-and-washing-machines).

Restricted vents can leave more heat and moisture in the laundry chase. That does not replace fixing the vent itself — and it is separate from duct cleaning — but many Chantilly townhome visits bundle both when the chase is overdue.

sections.heading: How to tell if your Chantilly system still carries builder dust
paragraphs: Not every dusty register in a 1990s–2000s house means original construction residue. These indicators are more specific:
listItems: Pull a supply register on the second floor. If the trunk walls show a white chalky base under darker surface dust, the builder load was never removed.

Run a damp finger along the inside of the trunk (safely, with power off and panels handled carefully). If the residue feels chalky/gritty rather than soft and fibrous, it often matches construction-style fines more than everyday household lint — a clue to inspect further, not a lab assay.
Check the air-handler cabinet for a manufacturer date — if it matches the house age and the evaporator coil has never been cleaned, the original dust layer extends into the coil housing.
Compare registers on opposite sides of the house: a noticeably darker film on the Route 28 side confirms corridor particulate is an active ongoing source.

sections.heading: Addressing a system that never got its first cleaning
paragraphs: A house that still carries builder dust needs a full trunk-and-branch cleaning, not just a filter swap. For Chantilly scheduling and flat-rate packages that include every register, visit the [Chantilly location page](/locations/chantilly). If the townhome dryer chase is part of the issue, [dryer vent cleaning](/dryer-vent-cleaning) can be bundled in the same appointment. Similar Dulles-corridor build-out patterns show up in our [Herndon construction dust](/blog/herndon-construction-dust-air-ducts) notes.
Call [(800) 606-3334](tel:8006063334) for Chantilly scheduling, or see [air duct cleaning](/air-duct-cleaning) and [Chantilly](/locations/chantilly).
listItems: After cleaning, upgrade from a MERV-8 panel filter to a MERV-11 pleated filter — this catches more of the sub-10-micron corridor particles before they re-enter the trunks.
Schedule dryer-chase cleaning annually in a stacked townhome; the compressed-lint risk is real and the access is already planned into the service visit.
If the HOA manages exterior dryer caps, confirm the cap model allows full brush access — some cap designs require removal for a thorough clean.
